title: Cardiorenal and cardiohepatic congestion in the context of tricuspid valve interventions
summary:
Patients with moderate to severe tricuspid regurgitation have an increased risk of death, regardless of whether they suffer from any other heart disease. This increased risk often arises from complications of the leaky valve, such as liver failure or kidney damage.

Drug treatment cannot improve the outlook for this type of valve failure, and open-heart surgery is often associated with a high risk of death. However, modern, minimally invasive procedures, such as repairing the valve using a catheter (known as TriClip™ or PASCAL®) or implanting special valve implants (such as TricValve®, EVOQUE, or VDYNE), are showing promising results. These methods reduce valve leakage and improve quality of life, while the risk of death during the procedure is significantly lower.

In our study, we want to examine how these different procedures affect liver and kidney function.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Indication for tricuspid valve intervention
(decision in interdisciplinary heart team)
- Optimal medical therapy for tricuspid regurgitation and any heart failure
- Consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
- Lack of patient consent
- Statutory Care
- Malignant tumor disease with an expected life expectancy of < 1 year
- Severe right ventricular systolic dysfunction (TAPSE <13mm)
- Severe pulmonary hypertension (PAPsys > 65mmHg)
- Left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 30%
- Untreated significant structural disease of the left ventricle, which should be treated as a matter of priority
- Permanent dialysis requirement 
- Contraindications to clip/prosthesis implantation 
-> Allergies to device components
-> Allergies to contrast agents or vitamin K antagonists
-> Deep vein thrombosis
-> Unsuitable anatomy
- Known tricuspid or mitral valve endocarditis in the last 12 months
- Psychiatric illness or behavioral disorder including alcohol and drug abuse. 
- Liver cirrhosis Child C
- Female patients of childbearing age
- Current participation in another study with an investigational drug or device that would directly affect the treatment or outcome of the current study
